title: Wage board: owners raise offer to Tk 15,700, workers ask Tk 22,000 as 481 factories halt
excerpt: The gap at the lowest grade is now Tk 6,300. BGMEA says production stopped at about 481 garment factories on Tuesday as protests spread.

image.alt: File photo: women garment workers at sewing machines on a factory floor in Bangladesh
image.credit: File photo: Fahad Faisal / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
Garment factory owners on Tuesday (24 November) raised their offer for the lowest-paid workers to Tk 15,700 a month, and the workers' side asked for Tk 22,000, the chairman of the Minimum Wage Board told reporters. The current minimum for entry-level (Grade IV) workers, set in 2023, is Tk 12,500.

Chairman Syed Azad Subhani said owners first offered Tk 15,000 for Grade IV, then Tk 15,500, and then Tk 15,700. The workers' side started at Tk 32,000 and came down to Tk 25,000 and then Tk 22,000. The meeting, the board's fourth, began at 2pm at its Segunbagicha office in Dhaka. Subhani said he hoped a final figure could be fixed the same evening.

The Business Standard published both sides' latest offers for all four grades:

  • Grade I: owners Tk 18,828, workers Tk 35,000 (now Tk 15,035)
  • Grade II: owners Tk 17,887, workers Tk 30,000 (now Tk 14,273)
  • Grade III: owners Tk 16,996, workers Tk 27,000 (now Tk 13,550)
  • Grade IV: owners Tk 15,700, workers Tk 22,000 (now Tk 12,500)

Production was halted at about 481 garment factories on Tuesday, a senior BGMEA leader told The Business Standard. He said 397 member factories had suspended work and another 84 had announced indefinite closures under Section 13(1) of the Labour Act. More than 400 of the affected factories are in Gazipur, with 62 in Savar and 18 in Mirpur.

Workers blocked the Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways in Gazipur, and police fired tear gas and sound grenades to disperse protesters in Gazipur and Ashulia. Prothom Alo reported that protesters vandalised and set fire to a police box on the highway and that 70 factories declared a holiday.

Why it matters

The minimum wage sets pay for garment workers, most of them women, for several years. The longer the board takes, the more factories close and the more pay workers lose. NGOs running legal aid, women workers' centres and health services in Gazipur, Savar and Ashulia are dealing with the effects now.

What to watch

Whether the board announces a figure tonight or tomorrow, whether workers accept it, and whether the 84 factories under Section 13(1) reopen. Devlens will update this story when the board announces its decision.

Correction

Devlens's story of 24 November said owners had offered Tk 15,800 on Monday, citing Prothom Alo. The wage board chairman said on Tuesday that the owners' offers for Grade IV were Tk 15,000, Tk 15,500 and Tk 15,700. That story has been corrected.
